newsitem.title: USA: Republic taking over Alamo in $625 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Republic taking over Alamo in $625 million deal.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc., moving to expand its automotive business, said Thursday it signed an agreement to take over Alamo-Rent-A-Car Inc. in a deal valued at $625 million.

Republic Industries is a diversified company led by businessman Wayne Huizenga that specializes in electronic security, solid waste and cars. The move follows the September collapse of Republic's planned acquisition of security firm ADT Ltd. Terms of the Alamo transaction were not immediately available. The companies said the deal will be accoounted for as a pooling of interests.
Huizenga said said Republic's AutoNation USA car business will benefit from Alamo's strong relationships with manufacturers and other automotive suppliers.

"The combination of Alamo with Republic's 'like-new' automobile retailing concept is an exceptional fit that will enable AutoNation USA to accelerate its business plan and create a unique, dedicated and predictable source of inventory for our megastore distribution system," Huizenga said in a statement.

Alamo is the fourth largest rental car company in the United States and operates a fleet of about 130,000 vehicles. Alamo operates in 42 states in the United States and has operations in 10 European countries and Canada.
Republic's stock jumped $2.50 to $33.25 on Nasdaq after the announcement.
